independent_assessment.practitioner_view: Solid plan for Titanic binary classification: Sex/Pclass/Age interactions are the canonical high-signal derivations, title extraction from Name is well-motivated, per-fold aggregates are correctly scoped. The main gap is has_cabin being described in prose but absent from all enumerated feature-group arrays, and n_features_planned=22 overcounts the 19 machine-readable entries. No leakage or coverage failures.

concerns_beyond_rules.concern: has_cabin binary flag is documented in derived_features_note and programmer_instructions but has no entry in any feature group array (direct_numeric, categorical_encoding, interactions, or summary_features). The programmer spec contract is incomplete for this feature.
concerns_beyond_rules.reasoning: The feature is planned in prose only. The programmer may implement it, but ablation gate and feature_spec.json will not formally track it unless it appears in an enumerated block. If dropped silently the informative missingness signal from Cabin (77.1% missing) is partially lost.

concerns_beyond_rules.concern: n_features_planned=22 does not match the 19 entries actually enumerated across all feature blocks (5 direct_numeric + 5 categorical_encoding + 5 per_fold_target_aggregates + 4 interactions). The discrepancy of 3 may reflect expected one-hot expansion columns (Sex→2, Embarked→3 = +3 net) but the schema says to count entries not expanded columns.
concerns_beyond_rules.reasoning: Misleads the modeling agent complexity calibration. The actual entry count is 19; the plan claims 22.

summary: No FAIL findings. Two WARNs: (1) has_cabin binary flag is planned in prose but absent from all enumerated feature-group arrays, leaving the ablation-gate spec contract incomplete for Cabin missingness signal; (2) n_features_planned=22 overcounts the 19 machine-readable entries by 3, likely from conflating one-hot expansion columns with entry counts.
